Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)
Searches: gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm", "GLM-5.3 speculative draft", "create_draft_parallel_config", "enable_expert_parallel draft model", gh pr list --state all --search "dflash", gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash".

#55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize hc_post, then hc_contract, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, --kv-cache-dtype auto, H100) main + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The model.py change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash’s mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its model.py hunk.
#55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft’s sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target’s MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; is_eagle_group follows use_eagle_block_drop(); tested with disable_eagle_block_drop=true). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
#56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None). If it merges first, this PR drops the speculative.py hunk.
#55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the kv_cache_utils.py part of this PR is superseded.
#54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks SupportsEagle3) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 start on main end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.
Due to discussion for kv cache allocation, this PR just submits the main support in advance.
Previous full supported performance
Setup. 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM main 9d4d9aa + this branch, V2 model runner (VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1). Target zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (fp8 weights, --kv-cache-dtype auto, --max-model-len 131072, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9, --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune, --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice). Draft incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).
Workload. 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (temperature=0), max_tokens=512, /v1/chat/completions. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. k = num_speculative_tokens, “FA” / “FI” = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is --max-num-seqs.

Takeaways:

num_speculative_tokens is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter’s block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
--max-num-seqs 96 vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423’s slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At --max-num-seqs 96 this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

Test Result
Unit tests. 3 passed (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).
pre-commit. All hooks pass on the five changed files, including mypy-3.10 (the follow-up commit fixes a dict invariance error in _get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next).
Startup. Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072), builds the KV cache (GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens), captures CUDA graphs and serves.
Tool-calling E2E against the running DFlash2 server (--tool-call-parser glm47, --reasoning-parser glm45): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.
Greedy output determinism. Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with temperature=0 the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.
Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626). Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the main layout, so it is a property of the target’s FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at --max-concurrency 1. Prefix caching is not involved (prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0 in every crash dump).
Known limitations / follow-ups

#55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; disable_eagle_block_drop was left at its default.
Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

Dovis01 (2026-09-24T11:18:28Z):
Thx for sharing ideas!
1. KV cache grouping
Following @ivanium’s reference commit, the DFlash drafter’s KV is now allocated as FullAttentionSpec and joins the target’s MLA/indexer UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs, while the GLM planner in kv_cache_utils.py no longer detects or promotes draft layers: it only accepts full-attention pages next to the MLA/indexer pages and sizes blocks from the attention group’s page_size_bytes, as in the reference. The difference is how the drafter gets that spec: instead of rewriting the draft architectures in Glm5NextModel.__init__ and patching get_kv_cache_spec on the attention instances, the target owns the policy through Glm5NextForCausalLM.adapt_draft_kv_cache_spec (sliding-window draft spec → FullAttentionSpec at the target block size, window kept for compute), which DraftModelSpeculator applies to the draft layers only when the V2 runner collects KV cache specs; the generic drafter (qwen3_dflash*.py) and the shared Attention layer stay untouched, so this is orthogonal to #50457. On 8×H100 (TP8) this gives 6 KV cache groups instead of 7 with the original separate draft group, and raises KV capacity from 1,359,138 to 1,542,574 tokens (+13.5%).
2. Upstream issue re-opened by this layout (#54374)
Booking the windowed drafter on full-attention pages silently re-opens #54374: with an MLA target the drafter is the only FlashAttention consumer, so FA3’s AOT split schedule stays on and acceptance collapses to ~1.0 under full CUDA graphs, because the guard in DFlashSpeculator.set_attn detects the window via get_kv_cache_spec_sliding_window, which only returns it for SlidingWindowSpec. Both the previous head 8c5a676 and the reference commit hit it, and it is easy to miss because copy-from-context prompts (needle, long documents) keep normal acceptance while generation-heavy requests collapse (outputs stay correct since verification is lossless).

0986790 makes the guard read the spec’s sliding_window attribute, as #54374 intended, and leaves get_kv_cache_spec_sliding_window unchanged since the KV cache manager and offloading use it for eviction semantics; a regression test covers it. On 8×H100 (TP8 + EP, k=6, full CUDA graphs), arithmetic prompts at concurrency 8 go from acceptance 1.21 / 375 tok/s with the reference to 5.68 / 1172 tok/s, the same short prompt needs 24 instead of 103 draft steps (acceptance 1.28 → 5.50), GSM8K-200 at concurrency 1 reaches accuracy 0.930 at 204.4 tok/s with acceptance 4.70, and needle prompts are unchanged (4.29 vs 4.25).

#57084 [Docs] Add PR checklist skill for coding agents
vllm-project/vllm#57084 · benchislett · MERGED · created 2026-09-15T22:22:05Z · merged 2026-09-30T21:47:29Z
Overview
(DISCLAIMER: I USED THE NEW SKILL TO HAVE GPT-6 AUTHOR THE PR DESCRIPTION BELOW, COMMIT THE CHANGES AND OPEN THIS PR. TREAT IT AS A REVIEWABLE EXAMPLE ARTIFACT. ALL CODE CHANGES WERE HAND WRITTEN WITH CARE BY ME.)
Add a pr-checklist skill for coding agents preparing, reviewing, or revising
vLLM pull requests. Integrate it with the agent contribution instructions and
the PR template.
Claims

Provide a structured review workflow covering design fit, compatibility,
complexity, tradeoffs, validation, test quality, code clarity, and PR evidence.
Distinguish validation performed for a contribution from tests maintained in
the repository, emphasizing meaningful coverage rather than test volume.
Include guidance for human-in-the-loop review and responding to prior feedback.
Require agents to use the skill before submission through AGENTS.md.
Restructure the PR template around Overview, Claims, Validation, and Details,
with checklist and AI-assistance disclosure fields.

The intended benefit is better-prepared contributions and less avoidable
maintainer follow-up. This PR does not claim a measured reduction in review
rounds or review time.
Validation
This change is documentation and agent instructions only. No serving-engine,
model, kernel, dependency, or runtime behavior is modified; runtime tests,
model evaluations, and performance benchmarks are not applicable.

Details
Motivation and research
The drafting process examined the latest 50 vLLM PRs reviewed by each of
benchislett and mgoin, ordered by the reviewer’s latest submitted review.

Restore causal sliding-window attention for image tokens in DeepSeek V4.1 VL.
V4.1 inherited the image visibility rules used by DeepSeek V4 Vision-Exp: tokens inside an image could attend to earlier image tokens outside the sliding window and to future image tokens. This differs from the official V4.1 reference implementation, where _window_kv uses get_window_topk_idxs and both image and text tokens attend to the same causal window. With a window of 128, query position p should see only [max(0, p - 127), p] through SWA.
The incorrect widening affects full-image prefill as well as continuation chunks. For example, at the beginning of image span [1900, 3948), the inherited rule exposes future image tokens through position 3947; the V4.1 reference permits only positions 1773 through 1900.
The key line in the official get_window_topk_idxs is:

idxs = torch.where(idxs > end, -1, idxs)
The reference masks every index greater than the query position with -1; this is a causal 128-token window, including the current token. Executing the published get_window_topk_idxs at query position 1900 produces exactly 128 indices, from 1773 through 1900, with no future positions.
Changes

Disable multimodal prefix-LM/bidirectional-range configuration for V4.1.
Make the shared SWA metadata builder respect an explicit is_mm_prefix_lm=False, keeping V4.1 metadata and paged indices causal.
Set the V4.1 attention-side image window extension to zero. Image preprocessing, the vision encoder, and vision_max_n_token remain unchanged.
Keep the existing causal gather lengths and workspace sizes. The final diff does not change NVIDIA or AMD workspace allocation.
Add six regression cases: full prefill and continuation prefill, each with compression ratios 0/1/2. Verify causal key positions in both gathered and paged indices, gather/CPU-plan consistency, and absence of image visibility extensions.

V4 Vision-Exp retains its existing image visibility behavior.
Validation
Run on GB200:

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  -k 'not test_builder_' -q --tb=short
Result: 30 passed, 3 deselected. The three existing builder tests require an inaccessible gated Hugging Face configuration. The new regression uses a local configuration and requires no model download.
Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. A local FlashMLA numerical sanity check also matched the causal reference, retaining a gather length of 227 and a first-query SWA length of 128 for seq_len=4000, query_len=100, and image span [1900, 3948).
Full-model VL accuracy, generation-length evaluation, and AMD runtime validation were not run. The evidence here establishes attention-window correctness at the metadata/kernel level.
Related work
Open-PR searches for SWA/gather, V4.1/prefill, and V4.1/causal/image found no other matching fix. #56986 concerns cross-layer compressed-KV gather reuse; it does not correct the image attention-window semantics addressed here.

Three things in the vendored code were intentional divergences, not schema, and are kept with their explanations:

Vision rms_norm_eps stays 1e-6. The checkpoint ships 1e-5 and upstream honours it; the vendored config force-overrode it because 1e-5 “produces repetitive/degraded image descriptions”. Now a named constant at its single call site.

Both vendored configs supplied a layers_block_type property that mapped their sparse-attention layer type onto "attention". Without it, ModelConfig.get_num_layers_by_block_type falls through to its layer_types branch, which only recognised "full_attention" — so both models would have counted zero attention layers. _get_full_attention_layer_indices in the turboquant config has the same blind spot, but it already checks layer_types first and so is unchanged by this PR. Flagging it as a separate pre-existing issue rather than widening scope here.
Open question: the frame sampler
This PR keeps vLLM’s own frame sampler, but I am not confident that is the right call and would like a view on it.
The sampler’s docstring justifies diverging from the reference implementation by noting that the linspace variant “cost 4 points on video grounding evals”. That comment describes only the short-clip branch (total_frames < extract_t), which requires fps < 2; I could not construct a case where that branch differs from upstream at all.
The branch that does differ is the common one, for an unrelated reason: vLLM walks at 1/(temporal_patch_size * target_fps) (0.25s), collecting ~2x the candidates, then re-spreads them with linspace. Upstream walks at 1/target_fps (0.5s) and keeps its picks. Over a sweep of realistic sources, 38/53 cases differ — same frame counts, different indices:

casevLLMupstream30s @30fps0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 76, 91, 1060, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 1053 frames @2fps0, 1, 2, 20, 1
vLLM’s spacing drifts off the target fps and short sources pick up a duplicated tail frame from the odd-parity pad. There is also no consistency argument for keeping our own: create_hf_metadata sets do_sample_frames = len(valid_frame_indices) == source.total_frames_num, so whenever the backend sub-samples the processor is told not to re-sample, and the backend’s choice is authoritative either way.
So switching to upstream’s sample_frames would delete the last vendored piece and looks more correct on the merits — but it changes frame selection for nearly every video, so it needs a video eval that I could not run. Keeping ours (what this PR does) preserves exactly what ships today at no eval cost. Happy to switch if a reviewer with a GPU wants to take the eval.
Dropped code left over from Qwen3-Next — please sanity-check
Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer selected between a MoE block and a dense Qwen3NextMLP:

This is a verbatim lift of qwen3_next.py:479-485, which arrived with the original support PR (#53896) — Qwen4Exp derives from Qwen3-Next and still subclasses Qwen3NextAttention and Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock. decoder_sparse_step and mlp_only_layers are Qwen3-Next concepts; upstream’s Qwen4ExpTextConfig declares neither, and neither appears anywhere in Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next or ...-FP8. They only resolved because the vendored config subclassed Qwen3NextConfig and inherited them, which is why nothing ever flagged the branch as dead.
Evaluating the original expression against both checkpoints with the old vendored config gives is_moe_layer True for 48/48 layers, no dense layers: with mlp_only_layers=[], num_experts=512 and decoder_sparse_step=1 it reduces to True for any layer index. Upstream’s qwen4_exp has no dense path at all (neither key appears in the model, and validate_architecture requires num_experts > 0), so such a checkpoint would not load in transformers either — which is why I think dropping it is right. #57407 [ROCm][Perf] Enable layer-aware CSA2 multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
vllm-project/vllm#57407 · shen-shanshan · MERGED · created 2026-09-17T15:42:14Z · merged 2026-09-27T15:48:02Z
Purpose
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has three attention layer shapes: full CSA2 layers (2/8/14/20) run SWA + compressor + indexer and build a new global KV cache with their own Top-K indices; reindex CSA2 layers (24/28/32/36) run SWA + indexer only, re-scoring Top-K over an earlier layer’s global KV cache; all other layers are dense or pure SWA.
The shared v4.1 pipeline overlaps the full CSA2 layers with three fork/join pairs per step (input projections; Q/SWA-insert vs compressor; indexer vs cache-insert) and the reindex layers with one. On ROCm each fork/join is a HIP event pair per side stream, so the multi-stream launch cost outweighs the overlap benefit there.

This PR gives the ROCm attention layer a layer-type-aware scheme with exactly one fork/join per step:
Full CSA2 layers (_forward_csa2_full): one 3-stream fork right after the input norm.

default stream: fused wqa+wkv → q/kv split+norm → wq_b → fused qnorm/RoPE/SWA-insert;
aux stream 0: the compressor chain (kv_score GEMM → save/compress/norm → RoPE-quant cache insert);
aux stream 1: indexer weights_proj.

After the single join, the indexer K write (_produce_k, whose wk consumes the aux-0 latent) and the query path (forward_q, whose wq_b consumes the default-stream qr) run serially, followed by the indexer op and sparse MLA.
Reindex CSA2 layers (_forward_csa2_reindex): the input projections run serially first (the query path consumes qr, so overlapping the weight projection is not worth it), then one 2-stream fork overlaps the SWA q path with the indexer query path.
Dense layers: fully serial (aux_stream_list disabled).

After the single join, the indexer K write (_produce_k, whose wk consumes the aux-0 latent) and the query path (forward_q, whose wq_b consumes the default-stream qr) run serially, followed by the indexer op and sparse MLA.
Reindex CSA2 layers (_forward_csa2_reindex): the input projections run serially first (the query path consumes qr, so overlapping the weight projection is not worth it), then one 2-stream fork overlaps the SWA q path with the indexer query path.
Dense layers: fully serial (aux_stream_list disabled).

A new shared helper execute_in_parallel_default_first (in vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py) mirrors execute_in_parallel but enqueues the default chain before the aux chains — the default chain is the longest, so starting it first shortens the step tail while the aux streams still only wait on the pre-fork default-stream work.
The fork is gated exactly like the shipped v4.0 multi-stream gate (#51794/#56853): it only runs where the fork/join becomes static graph edges (inside capture, or with non-dict metadata such as the profile run); everywhere else — including MRV1, which keeps its wide eager region (#51430) — the layer falls back to the fully sequential base pipeline.
The CUDA/NVIDIA path is untouched except for a behavior-neutral base refactor: the v4.1 indexer’s query path is extracted into DeepseekV4Indexer.forward_q, still driven unchanged by the base forward (_produce_k keeps its private name). This is not a duplicate of #51794/#56853, which cover v4.0: v4.1-flash has a different topology (the indexer derives K from the kv-source compressor’s latent, with no indexer-local compressor), so the overlap must differ per layer type.

vllm-project/vllm#57497 · mrodden · MERGED · created 2026-09-18T05:04:02Z · merged 2026-09-25T04:28:20Z
Purpose

Enable VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD on the AMD/ROCm path: keep the Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram table in pinned host memory, read through a UVA view on the GPU.
Free VRAM so Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (FP8 table ~51 GiB) / Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (bf16 table ~102 GiB) serve on one MI300X with the table entirely in host RAM.
Keep the pinned lookup behind a custom op (qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding_pinned) with mutates_args=["output"] so the large embedding weight is never materialized by torch.compile (Inductor autotuning builds a bf16 copy of the table during compile, which OOMs on AMD setups without enough VRAM) and the op survives aot_autograd/Inductor.
Move the PLE embedding storage classes to qwen4_exp/common so the AMD and NVIDIA paths share one implementation (NVIDIA re-exports).
Relax the PLE enable gate to is_cuda_alike() so ROCm is accepted, matching the existing NVIDIA default (VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD defaults on for both; =0 opts out). Also, my local testing shows little to no performance loss for PLE offload while saving a good chunk of VRAM for more KV cache.
Why this is not duplicating existing PRs:

#54371 (merged — source of the UVA offload code, ported here)
#55040 (AMD FP8 PLE, different approach: FP8 storage + forward dequant vs load-time bf16 fold; no offload/prefetch)
#55334 / #54070 / #54129 (nvidia + mmap — complementary).

Reproducing the pinned-id hazard on the downstream gfx906 fork (4x MI50) — worth folding in before the pinned path gets wider use.
We adopted the PLE n-gram offload (mmap’d host shards on our side) for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and hit two producer classes in the id-staging path that a strict guard cannot enumerate:

Sentinel producers. The spec-decode drafter pre-fills sample_idx_mapping with -1 for slots holding no real sample, and that tensor reaches the n-gram lookup on every MTP drafter warmup/capture pass. A raise-on-out-of-range guard killed two boots at propose() -> PLE embedding.
Unwritten pinned buffers (capture path). With speculative decoding + CUDA graphs, the lookup ran with capture-time inputs and produced 0xff80ff80ff80ff80 repeated (min == max) on the compile/graph path only — --enforce-eager hides it entirely.

A guard that refuses is itself a boot-breaker (third failure of the day: fold the sentinel, keep the raise, still died). What we converged on:

A guard that refuses is itself a boot-breaker (third failure of the day: fold the sentinel, keep the raise, still died). What we converged on:

Fold-and-warn by default: one host-side range test over the whole id tensor before the shard loop; every out-of-range id folds onto row 0, with a warn-once per module carrying the span and the count; a strict env var restores the raise.
Fold, don’t clamp: clamping a large positive id lands on the last row — a real embedding and therefore a plausible wrong answer. Row 0 costs one wrong row for slots whose outputs are discarded anyway.

The general lesson we took: a guard that can refuse a boot must be justified against producers it cannot enumerate — warn-and-fold by default, raise behind a flag. (Where the provider keeps the lookup out of the captured region entirely — our final form — the fold becomes defensive rather than load-bearing, but anyone on the graph path without that split will hit class 2.)
If useful, the 24-test harness (fold/warn/strict paths, nesting, exception path, state restore) can be shared. Context: KIntegrated/vllm-gfx906-mobydick (gfx906 QSA-FN train); the pinned path here stages ids the same way.

#57632 [DFlash] Capture the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph
vllm-project/vllm#57632 · Juntian777 · MERGED · created 2026-09-18T21:17:51Z · merged 2026-09-24T21:38:04Z
Purpose
Even when the query forward replays a FULL CUDA graph, the DFlash/DSpark draft step still runs the context K/V precompute (precompute_and_store_context_kv) eagerly outside the graph, because the number of context tokens varies from step to step.
This PR captures the context K/V precompute ahead of the query forward in the draft’s FULL decode graph. Each graph stores one full verify of context rows per request; rows past the batch are padded with PAD_SLOT_ID so they write no K/V, and any prefill context beyond the graph’s rows is stored eagerly before replay. The precompute has no host syncs, so every DFlash drafter captures it. The draft attention metadata build stays eager, as before.
Validation
Capturing the context K/V precompute must not change the speculator’s proposals. The checks below therefore compare acceptance and accuracy between this branch’s parent commit (c723a831a8) and d8de1d3a2f, and serving performance against current main, with everything else held fixed.

Fuse TP all-reduce, mHC post mixing, delayed collapse, and RMSNorm at DSV4.1 decoder boundaries. This replaces three launches with one, preserves the BF16 boundaries, and retains coefficient overlap. The kernel reuses the existing MNNVL workspace without an additional persistent communication allocation.
Enabled by default for eligible SM100 TP4 forwards with 1–16 tokens, including speculative decoding. The selector requires hidden size 5120, hc_mult=4, EP disabled, and a multicast workspace; it does not restrict DP/PP size, LoRA, or attention backend. The existing overlap-support checks still apply, including disabling overlap for ubatching. Larger batches and graph boundaries use the existing operations. Sixteen is the largest size with a validated gain, not a measured crossover.
Builds on #57603, now merged into main, which overlaps coefficient computation but does not fuse collectives. This differs from #51244’s terminal mHC/head fusion. Open-PR searches for mhc allreduce and mhc fusion found no duplicate of this decoder-boundary collective fusion.
The independent startup warmup fixes have been extracted: DeepGEMM mHC projection coverage is in #57843, and cached FlashInfer MXFP8 tactics are in #57842. Neither is included in this fusion PR.
Communication choice and token cutoff
Keep multicast and the 16-token cutoff. A controlled GB200 TP4 experiment replaced multicast stores with explicit stores to each of the four peers, retaining the same math, Lamport synchronization, cleanup, and PDL. Push did not consistently improve performance:

Extending fusion to 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 tokens regressed model-forward time in this screen, despite isolated kernel gains; coefficient overlap remained disabled above 16. Some nonstandard sizes used default tactics because exact cache buckets were absent. A follow-up using normal serving autotune buckets confirmed the gain at 1 and 16 tokens (4.667→4.060 ms and 7.783→7.127 ms). Near-boundary runs at 17 and 20 tokens failed the unfused baseline’s native-top-k correctness check, so no timings from those shapes are accepted. This supports retaining 16 conservatively; it does not establish the exact crossover. No new model accuracy evaluation was run for the experimental variants.
Multicast requires a supported NVLink/NVSwitch configuration and successful group memory setup; GPU generation alone does not establish support. Explicit peer stores could broaden support to Hopper-or-newer systems with suitable peer-memory access without multicast. That would require separate allocation/dispatch support and hardware validation: this PR remains SM100 TP4, and the experimental push variant reused the existing workspace. Push is a possible portability fallback, not a demonstrated GB200 performance improvement.

Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank.
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py
Building on top of @almogtavor ‘s work vllm-project/vllm#50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include,

SlidingWindowMLASpec
Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
models.

Notably,

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and
zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category.

Changes:

AttentionSpec.max_tp_shards: int | None = None: how many distinct shards this cache splits into across TP. A value of means, all TP ranks are replicas. None means unknown and is treated as not replicated.

It’s opt-in: no spec class has a default that claims replication, so a layer that forgets it only loses dedup, never correctness. This is the same pattern as MambaSpec.tp_replicated.
max_tp_shards=1 is set only where the cache has been checked to be identical on every TP rank:

generic MLAAttention (mla_attention.py), which covers the DSv3 / V3.2 / GLM-5.3 latent cache;
the DSv3.2 indexer cache (deepseek_v2.py; wk_weights_proj uses disable_tp=True);
DeepSeek-V4 attention and indexer caches (deepseek_v4/attention.py);
the DeepSeek-V4 compressor state (fused_wkv_wgate uses disable_tp=True);
the DeepSeek-V4 SWA cache (sparse_swa.py).

generic MLAAttention (mla_attention.py), which covers the DSv3 / V3.2 / GLM-5.3 latent cache;
the DSv3.2 indexer cache (deepseek_v2.py; wk_weights_proj uses disable_tp=True);
DeepSeek-V4 attention and indexer caches (deepseek_v4/attention.py);
the DeepSeek-V4 compressor state (fused_wkv_wgate uses disable_tp=True);
the DeepSeek-V4 SWA cache (sparse_swa.py).




KVCacheConfig.kv_tp_replicas: int = 1 : get_kv_cache_configs sets it through kv_cache_groups_tp_replicas(groups, tp_size, dcp_size) - The gcd of each layer’s tp_size // max_tp_shards, taken per layer through iter_layer_specs. A layer counts as 1 if it isn’t an attention spec, has no value set, or is DCP-sharded under DCP.
Offloading: replicated_layout requires tp > 1 and kv_tp_replicas == tp. T

Justification for adding a KVCacheConfig member
MLAAttentionSpec shares uniform_type_base_spec=FullAttentionSpec, so one UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs group can mix MLA and GQA layers. generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config keeps an arbitrary layer spec, so the value has to be computed before that. Otherwise the scheduler could see an MLA spec and wrongly de-duplicate head-sharded KV.

#57906 [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm
vllm-project/vllm#57906 · Fangzhou-Ai · MERGED · created 2026-09-21T08:07:25Z · merged 2026-09-21T10:29:15Z
Purpose
Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm, where it currently faults the GPU.
SWA bounded replay (#56227, on by default) keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching and rebuilds it after a prefix hit by padding the replayed tokens’ slots in the prefix-cacheable groups. Correctness depends on the consuming prefill kernel clamping the window; that clamp landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA paths.
The ROCm sparse SWA metadata builders (DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder in both deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py and deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py) only gained the replay_start kwarg and forward it to the base builder. Nothing on the ROCm prefill path clamps the window, so the first prefix hit that carries a replay start walks off the padded slots and raises HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT, which takes down the worker and then the engine core:

Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x5621a810) on address 0x7ba8c13ff000. Reason: Unknown.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'
RuntimeError: Engine core process EngineCore died unexpectedly.

Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x5621a810) on address 0x7ba8c13ff000. Reason: Unknown.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'
RuntimeError: Engine core process EngineCore died unexpectedly.

This adds a ROCm guard alongside the existing model-runner-V2 and prefill-context-parallel guards in DeepseekV4Attention. Prefix caching itself is unaffected — the sliding-window cache simply takes part in it again, which is the pre-#56227 behavior. The guard should be removed once the ROCm prefill kernels clamp the window too.
Test Plan
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, TP=4, --max-model-len 1048576, --max-num-batched-tokens 16384, DSpark speculative decoding, --moe-backend aiter.

vllm-project/vllm#57934 · askliar · MERGED · created 2026-09-21T11:43:20Z · merged 2026-09-25T14:08:29Z
What changes
Add LiLiCorrDraftModel (2608.20530⁠ (Rusanovsky et al., 2026) ) to the existing MRV2 DFlash path. The exported SGLang head reranks global candidate lattices using target embeddings, full-vocabulary log probabilities, draft hidden states and the normalized last committed target context. Both plain and grouped-convolution checkpoints are supported.
The port reuses DFlash2 convolution layers and extracts its existing candidate walk/cache orchestration into a shared helper. Greedy and probabilistic drafting use the current vLLM sampling and rejection machinery. No new scheduler, attention backend or verification algorithm is introduced. Correlator and convolution projections use the draft quantization configuration except for lattice QKV and the split-factor/fused-edge projections. Those retain floating-point weights and F.linear; factor_input_proj, out_head and in_head must be excluded during export. Reduced draft vocabularies are outside this scope.
ModelOpt exclusions use checkpoint-local draft layer numbers, while vLLM assigns global runtime layer numbers to draft attention layers. The quantization config now retains its exported exclusions and adds runtime-index aliases before constructing the draft layers. This lets mixed BF16/NVFP4 variants allocate the correct linear method without changing checkpoint names or attention/KV layer identity.
References: SGLang sgl-project/sglang#37462, DSpark vllm-project/vllm#46995, DFlash2 vllm-project/vllm#52816.

More and more frontend PRs are written and reviewed by coding agents. Asked “is this a bug or intended?” or “what should this default to?”, they answer from memory or from vLLM’s own code. But vLLM’s code is the thing under test, so that reasoning approves drift instead of catching it.
What this PR adds. A check-api-compat skill. Agents load it on their own for any change, review or question touching /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings or /v1/messages. It tells the agent to:

Read upstream, not vLLM. Sources are, in order: the OpenAI OpenAPI YAML, the installed openai SDK types, then the docs. For Anthropic: the Messages docs, then the anthropic SDK types. The agent records which source and version answered.
Read both sides of a field in vLLM. An endpoint → protocol.py / serving.py / api_router.py map points the agent at the code that uses a field, not just where it is declared. A field that is declared correctly but silently ignored still counts as a bug.
Compare on name, type, default and semantics, plus streaming terminators, error bodies and omitted-vs-null.
Classify before reporting. Each finding is one of:

matches upstream
vLLM extension: allowed, e.g. vllm_xargs, min_p
incompatibility: reported with the upstream source and the vLLM file:line

#58132 [Model] Decoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1
vllm-project/vllm#58132 · ivanium · MERGED · created 2026-09-22T10:07:47Z · merged 2026-09-29T08:25:47Z
Purpose
Decoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1, on top of the encoder side (#56227). The layers past the last KV-source layer (21-39 of 40 on V4.1-Flash) own only sliding-window KV, so in eager prefill steps they run on each request’s last 128 tokens, cold prefills included. Simplified re-submission of #56752 (closed); no other open PR implements this.

DeepseekV41ModelState.prepare_attn prepares the kept rows as a sub-batch, the way a microbatch is prepared: one Triton kernel gathers rows, positions, slot mappings and the replay-layer KV start, and the sub-batch gets attention metadata and a forward context of its own. DP ranks agree on whether any rank trims and on every rank’s replay token count.
DecoderReplayLayers gathers the layer inputs by those rows, runs the replay layers under that context and scatters the outputs back.
Only eager steps trim. A step that fits a CUDA graph (up to 1024 tokens by default) keeps the replay layers on its whole batch inside the graph: such steps are launch-bound, so the graph is worth more than the trim. prepare_attn already gets the step’s graph mode, which DP ranks share, so there are no nested captures, no eager breaks and no runner changes; the diff is confined to vllm/models/deepseek_v41/, a config docstring and the CI job list.
With the fused MoE finalize of #58586, a decode step’s cut layer hands its unfinalized MoEOutput to the replay layers unchanged, and layer 21’s first boundary finalizes it. A trimming step holds a prefill longer than the window, more tokens than any step that defers its finalize, so the trim path only sees tensors.
Stays off, with a warning, when the PP stage does not hold every layer after the cut, under sequence-parallel MoE, PCP or microbatching, with an Engram layer after the cut, or with a drafter window wider than the target’s. --no-swa-bounded-replay turns off both sides. A no-op on ROCm.

#58180 [Agents] Add model-optimization skill with performance goal matrix
vllm-project/vllm#58180 · faradawn · CLOSED · created 2026-09-22T16:11:52Z · merged 
Overview
“Optimize this model” is not an actionable instruction for a coding agent, and
it is roughly what agents are given today. It does not say which parallelism to
tune, which serving regime and request shape to tune for, which harness defines
the number, or whether the target is throughput or perf/W. Agents therefore pick
a cell implicitly, optimize it, and report a win that does not hold in the
configuration the maintainer cares about.
This adds a model-optimization skill under .agents/skills/ that forces those
five choices to be made and stated before any code changes, anchored on a
performance goal matrix of parallelism x regime x shape. It also bundles a
mergify rule so the existing agents label is actually applied to agent
instruction and skill changes.
Related: #57084 (pr-checklist skill, whose template and checklist this
description follows).
Claims

A skill that converts a vague optimization request into a single named goal:
parallelism (TP, TP+EP, DP+EP, DCP, PCP+EP), regime (decode / prefill /
mixed), shape (concurrency and KV or prompt length), harness, and metric.

#58358 [Rust Frontend] Token-aware marker parsing for Kimi K3
vllm-project/vllm#58358 · BugenZhao · MERGED · created 2026-09-23T13:06:29Z · merged 2026-10-01T04:21:52Z
Purpose
Kimi K3 delimits channels with dedicated special tokens (<|open|>, <|close|>, <|sep|>, <|end_of_msg|>), but the model can also spell the same bytes with ordinary BPE tokens, for example while quoting an XTML snippet in its reasoning. The Rust K3 unified parser matched markers by decoded text only, so an ordinary <|close|>think<|sep|> inside reasoning closed the think channel early, and the rest of the message landed in the wrong channel or was dropped, with no error surfaced to the client.
This PR makes K3 channel boundaries token-aware using the per-token attribution that already reaches unified parsers through DecodedText: a marker’s special-token segments count as structure only when a single token with the expected ID produced them. Equal text from ordinary tokens stays content in the current channel. Text stays the parse axis, so marker words (think, response, call) and tag attributes are still matched by spelling.
Stacked on #58357, which anchors a token that follows an incomplete UTF-8 byte at its own first byte. Without it, a genuine special token right after such a byte is anchored too early and would not be recognized as structural. #58357 in turn sits on #59048, which makes the chat roundtrip harness and the parser benchmarks feed attributed input like the serving path.
Changes:

Parser utils: Attributed<'i, M> is a winnow stream (Stateful<Partial<LocatingSlice<&str>>, _>) over the buffer that carries its token anchors and the parser’s markers, so existing combinators work unchanged and grammar functions read the markers through input.markers() instead of an extra parameter. Marker is a marker spelling whose special-token segments are guarded by SpecialToken (spelling and ID resolved together); the same definition drives both the consuming parser and the safe-text scanner, so they cannot disagree. MarkerStream is implemented for Partial<&str> and Attributed, and one generic scanner serves both. Guarded markers take candidates from token anchors, so an ordinary lookalike never causes hold-back, including a partial …<|clo at the buffer tail. Existing text-only parsers keep passing &[&str] to the same helpers and have no diff; token-aware parsers call parse_buffered_event_attributed(&DecodedText, ..) instead of parse_buffered_event(&str, ..).
Kimi K3: all channel boundaries, call open/close, and the separator ending call attributes are structural. The parser requires token-attributed input, which the vLLM chat path provides; fed unattributed text, it treats every marker as content. There is no text-only fallback mode: Marker::without_guards keeps one cheap to add if an integrator without attribution needs it. <|end_of_msg|> is now required like the other structural tokens.

Known limitations, left for follow-ups:

argument and json blocks inside a completed call body are still parsed from text, so a string argument that literally contains <|close|>argument<|sep|> is still ambiguous, as before.
The K3 output grammar (structural tags) is still text-level, so under a constrained decode it can treat an ordinary lookalike as a boundary while the parser keeps it as content. XGrammar’s token formats can express the structural positions; that is a separate change.

#58489 [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Keep pinned PLE prefetch ids out of the CUDA graph pool
vllm-project/vllm#58489 · Juntian777 · MERGED · created 2026-09-24T01:47:40Z · merged 2026-09-25T02:51:51Z
Problem and fix
Fixes #58441. With engram_config.cpu_offload=True, Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding.start_prefetch launches the PLE lookup on a side stream and returns; _finalize_prefetch joins it one decoder layer later. Qwen4Exp defaults to breakable CUDA graphs, so for PIECEWISE batches (prefill/mixed batches up to the capture size, or every batch with cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE) start_prefetch is an eager break and its arguments are replaced by weak_ref_tensors. Two things then combine:

gathered_ids.record_stream(prefetch_stream) is a no-op: with etp_data_parallel_size == 1, gathered_ids is the weak ref itself, and the caching allocator skips recordStream for storage it does not own.
The only strong reference to the ids is the local ngram_ids in Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding.start_prefetch, which drops as soon as it returns, while the next segment is already being captured. The graph-pool block goes straight back to the free list and the rest of the preceding decoder layer can be captured on top of it.

At replay the side stream reads the ids while the main stream may be overwriting them, so greedy outputs silently stop being reproducible.
The fix computes the prefetch ids into a persistent per-layer buffer through the existing output= argument of compute_ngram_ids. This mirrors the persistent _prefetch_buffer already used for the lookup output, adds no kernel or copy, and costs max_num_batched_tokens * ngram_heads * 8 bytes per PLE layer. FULL graphs and eager runs were already safe (the argument stays a real tensor there), and ETP spanning DP is unaffected (the ids are re-gathered into a fresh tensor inside the eager break).
Validation

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py

51 passed on GB200. The new test_ngram_prefetch_ids_outlive_start_prefetch reproduces the lifetime bug without a full graph capture: the prefetch stub keeps a weak ref to the ids, as the eager break does, and a fresh MemPool makes the next same-size allocation reuse freed storage, as a later graph segment would. On main the weak ref reads the overwritten -1s (3/3 runs); with this change it reads the reference ids.
Pre-commit passed.
No model eval: the ids are produced by the same kernel into a different buffer, so outputs only change where the race corrupted them. The reporter’s cold/warm greedy table in #58441 (8/8 identical once the ids are in a persistent buffer) covers the end-to-end effect.

_ring_slot_mapping_kernel (vllm/models/deepseek_v41/compressor.py) maps each token to block_table[req, 0] * capacity + pos % capacity. Warmup and CUDA-graph capture run dummy batches whose block tables are zeroed, so their compressor state rows are written into block 0. That is the null block, and every KV-cache group shares it. The fp32 state bytes therefore land in other layers’ pages. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, layer 2’s ring overlaps the sliding-window KV of layers 0–13, and layer 8’s overlaps layers 0–27.
Why it matters: sparse MLA decode kernels gather the null block for masked candidates and weight it by zero. When the bytes decode to a non-finite value, 0 × NaN is still NaN. On sm_120 (FlashInfer’s DSv4 sparse decode) with DSpark speculative decoding and FULL CUDA graphs, this produced wrong outputs on the first request (0 accepted drafts), then cudaErrorIllegalAddress / Xid 31 MMU faults on the next prefill.
The bug is latent without DSpark too: block 0 still ends dirty (we measured 29 NaN bytes). It used to be masked because warmup_kernels ran after capture_model, and that warmup zeroed block 0 again. gpu_worker.py now runs warmup_kernels before capture_model, so the bytes survive into serving.
The fix maps tokens whose ring block is 0 to PAD (-1), which the ring consumers already skip. Real requests never own block 0, so their mapping is unchanged.

New test_v41_compressor_ring_never_writes_the_null_block, next to the existing test_v41_compressor_metadata_maps_tokens_to_their_ring: a dummy request on block 0 must map to PAD, and a real request next to it must keep its ring slots.

Both tests pass with the fix. As a control, the new test fails without it: assert [0, 1, 25, 26] == [-1, -1, 25, 26], i.e. the dummy tokens are written to slots 0 and 1 of the null block. without the fix: block 0 of every sliding-window layer is non-finite after capture, the first request decodes garbage, and the next ~1.6k-token prefill raises Xid 31;
with the fix: all 13 block-0 views stay clean through capture and 11,000 decode steps (including c16 load); needle retrieval 9/9, greedy determinism and shared-prefix divergence checks pass; 0 Xid; c1 131 tok/s, c16 672 tok/s, DSpark acceptance 0.38.

#58671 [ROCm][DSv4.1] Paged MXFP4 sparse indexer on aiter’s MQA-logits kernel
vllm-project/vllm#58671 · cagrikymk · MERGED · created 2026-09-25T06:22:52Z · merged 2026-09-29T06:37:58Z
Summary
Adds a ROCm (gfx950) path for DeepSeek V4.1’s indexer with an MXFP4 K cache, built on aiter’s paged MXFP4 MQA-logits Gluon kernel. The CUDA path is unchanged. There are two modes:

Regular MXFP4 (indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"): dense logits over the whole context, read straight from the paged K cache.
Sparse MXFP4 (opt-in, also set indexer_sparse_logits=True): the candidate source takes block maxima from the same pass that writes its logits, and the consumer layers score only the candidate pool instead of the whole context. Steps whose contexts are too short for the pool to pay off keep the regular pass, so it helps mainly at long contexts.

Both modes:

The logits kernel reads the preshuffled paged K cache in place, so no K gather is needed, prefill included.
K is written to the cache by aiter’s k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache, and Q is quantized by q_rope_mxfp4_quant.
Each prefill chunk is packed into one launch through query_start_loc. Uniform spec-decode steps run as next_n-row sequences, with the decode schedule built once per step.
128-token KV pages are preferred.

In sparse mode, the candidate pool is resolved once per step and shared by every consumer layer.

#58814 [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Refresh DSpark context KV cache pointers after the KV cache is re-bound
vllm-project/vllm#58814 · okorzh-amd · MERGED · created 2026-09-26T02:12:19Z · merged 2026-09-28T16:05:11Z
##Purpose
Fixes a GPU memory fault and silent memory corruption in the Kimi-K3 DSpark draft, introduced by #57632.

21:05:36  JIT kernel warmup finished            (all 8 ranks)
          Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT
          Memory access fault by GPU node-14 ... on address 0x7ec3c95b0000. Reason: Unknown.
21:15:38  [Rank 0..7] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: _ALLGATHER_BASE ... 600000 ms
          RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed

K3DSparkModel caches the per-layer KV cache base pointers, and the block-layout flag, on first use and never rebuilds them. Since #57632 captures the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph, that first use now happens during the CUDA graph memory-profiling capture. That capture runs against a temporary KV cache that is freed afterwards. The real KV cache is then allocated at different addresses, but the draft keeps the stale pointers, so every later context K/V insert writes into freed memory.
This change keys both cached values on the live kv_cache.data_ptr() tuple and rebuilds them when it changes. The pointer array is updated in place, so captured graphs keep reading live pointers. The rebuild only runs on eager calls; an assert guards against it running during capture.
kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py is the only K3 DSpark implementation and is used on every platform, so this also applies to CUDA. It was only tested on ROCm.

#58961 [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Release the profiling KV cache held by QSA key views
vllm-project/vllm#58961 · lucifer1004 · MERGED · created 2026-09-28T03:17:19Z · merged 2026-09-28T08:11:47Z
Purpose
Fixes #58960.
QSAKeyStateCache.bind_kv_cache stored the views key_cache and rope_position_cache next to kv_cache. clear_layer_kv_caches only resets kv_cache, so after CUDA graph memory profiling these views kept the profiling KV cache alive (9.76 GiB for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 at TP2) past _teardown_profiling_state()’s empty_cache(). It was freed only in the real initialize_kv_cache, stayed cached, and a later long-lived allocation pinned the block. FULL CUDA graph capture then ran out of memory at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 with 9.38 GiB free but unreleasable in the default pool. The issue has the memory-snapshot evidence.
The change derives both views from kv_cache on access, so kv_cache is the only reference to the bound storage, the same contract Mamba layers follow. Read sites (indexer_qsa.py on NVIDIA and AMD) are unchanged; they get the same tensor views as before.
Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue covers QSA cache lifetime or profiling teardown for Qwen4Exp. #58439 and #58815 change Qwen4Exp PLE storage, not the QSA cache; #46515 fixes a different leak during CUDA graph memory profiling.

#59069 [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Fuse AttnRes output with per-token FP8 input quantization
vllm-project/vllm#59069 · whx-sjtu · MERGED · created 2026-09-28T16:23:18Z · merged 2026-10-08T12:01:48Z
Summary
Eligible Kimi-K3 AMD AttnRes outputs currently materialize BF16 activations that the next linear immediately quantizes. Fuse that per-token FP8 conversion into AttnRes and pass native QuantizedActivation to supported consumers.

 AttnRes + output RMSNorm
-  store BF16 → per-token FP8 quant → input GEMM
+  store FP8 + scale → input GEMM
Enable the path only for kFp8DynamicTokenSym and only when all consumers accept the same key. Mixed MoE/router consumers, unsupported linear kernels, and batch-invariant mode retain the original path. Preserve BF16 rounding before quantization and the prefix/block write contract.
This is independent of PD connector work and targets main. Duplicate checks covered #50682, #52968, and #53154: #52968’s current diff covers convolution and sigmoid/multiply; #53154 covers MXFP4 output fusions. This PR supplies AttnRes per-token FP8 inputs. The current rowwise Torch FP8 KDA kernel does not expose the required input capability, so this PR does not claim all KDA inputs are fused.
Evidence
CI follow-up (2026-10-08)
Buildkite #93497 exposed an implicit compiled reference in the FP8 output test when AITER is disabled. Commit 42f0ad593 sets compile_native=False for the QuantFP8 reference, keeping its rounding independent of Inductor fusion. Production code and every numerical tolerance are unchanged. The AttnRes and MLA/KDA direct-return suites pass with AITER disabled (23 passed) and enabled (23 passed); changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. Buildkite #93546 retries the failed K3 step on that commit.

Before: AttnRes and per-token quantization launch separately.
After: A single producer emits activation and scale. Existing + new AttnRes cases passed on all eight MI355X GPUs (16 tests/rank in the final run, including the three capability cases), with exact prefix/block writes, scale rtol 1e-6, and rounding differences limited to an adjacent FP8 code in <1e-4 of values. Three direct-return tests also passed.
In the paired rank-0 prefill trace, the corresponding standalone AITER per-token quant kernel count falls from 4009 to 3078 (931 calls removed), while AttnRes executes the same 3553 calls.
pre-commit run and pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual: passed.
Eight-rank benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_amd_fp8_fusions.py compares AttnRes + quant + one MLA input GEMM (N2112/K7168), using nine rotated CUDA-graph samples per rank. Median of per-rank medians, four residual blocks:

Paired full-model integration validation used the same eight MI355X GPUs, TP8/DCP8, DSpark3 with natural/standard rejection, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 80 sequences / 16384 batched tokens / 1048576 context. The candidate adds both this PR and the companion DCP prefill fusion #59070 to an exact saved diagnostic baseline; the following model results are combined, not isolated attribution to this PR.

Three unprofiled repetitions of the same eight-case prefix chain: all 24 first-token outputs, cache-hit counts and computed-token counts match. #59119 [DSv4.1] Avoid runtime recompiles of _ring_slot_mapping_kernel
vllm-project/vllm#59119 · Juntian777 · MERGED · created 2026-09-29T02:25:30Z · merged 2026-09-29T07:31:30Z
Summary
_ring_slot_mapping_kernel builds the compressor ring slot mapping in CompressorMetadataBuilder.build() and runs on every step. Its int args num_tokens and num_actual_tokens change from step to step, and Triton specializes int args by value (== 1, % 16 == 0, or neither), so each new combination compiles a new variant while serving. These compiles are not covered by startup warmup because the triggering combinations depend on the live batch (for example, a real token count that is a multiple of 16 padded to one that is not). Under DP/EP, a rank that stops to compile stalls every other rank at the next collective.
This PR marks block_table_stride, num_actual_tokens and num_tokens as do_not_specialize, so one variant is compiled at startup and reused for every batch. These args only feed address and mask arithmetic; dropping their divisibility hints narrows some loads/stores, but the kernel is latency-bound on its dependent loads and performance is unchanged (see below).
Evidence from a DSv4.1-Flash DEP4 AgentX run on GB200: a new variant of this kernel was compiled 46 min after the server was healthy, in the middle of a benchmark, and the Triton cache holds 6 variants of it.
This does not overlap with #58560, which changes the kernel’s store mask (null block), not its specialization.

#59197 [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Skip SWA bounded replay for KV loads that carry the window
vllm-project/vllm#59197 · ivanium · MERGED · created 2026-09-29T09:53:46Z · merged 2026-10-07T22:28:43Z
Also credit to @wangyicong52 who originally reported the issue and helped test the PR.
Purpose
SWA bounded replay (#56227) replays the last window of every prefix hit, including KV loaded by P/D connectors, which transfer the request’s own sliding-window KV. P/D decode on DeepSeek-V4.1 therefore recomputed the last 128 prompt tokens of every request. The whole-block rounding that replay applies to external hits also shrinks decode’s allocation below what prefill exports, so NIXL’s end-aligned pairing puts prefill block k + 1 into decode block k for the MLA groups whenever N % 128 != 0 (found with a CPU probe of the real scheduler and NIXL code).
Changes


The scheduler takes a load that restores every replayed group (get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids, added by #59504) as is: no replay, no whole-block rounding, and no dropping of hits no longer than the window. Async loads record the decision at admission and apply it when the KV arrives; failed loads and store / offloading loads still replay.


Without the replay, decode relies on the transferred window as laid out, so NIXL and Mooncake now back off the last prompt token for models with bounded replay, as they already do for Mamba: prefill stops at N - 1, decode loads N - 1 tokens and computes the last one. Loading all N tokens and rewinding one after laying the window out for N dropped the block holding position N - W when N % block_size == block_size - 1, and the recomputed token attended to the null block, which DeepSeek-V4.1 does not keep zero.

Loading all N tokens and rewinding one after laying the window out for N dropped the block holding position N - W when N % block_size == block_size - 1, and the recomputed token attended to the null block, which DeepSeek-V4.1 does not keep zero.


The prompt cut keeps two prompt-indexed features working (they were already broken for Mamba P/D): a request with prompt logprobs (e.g. completions with echo and logprobs) is not cut, since it skips reading the prefix cache and the decoder never loads its KV; before, the prefiller returned prompt logprobs for one token fewer than the prompt and the frontend failed. The routed-experts (R3) start is clamped to the prompt length; a start equal to the original length lay past the cut prompt and made the scheduler assert.


This PR stands alone. #59330 is the general fix: it applies the backoff to every model (a sliding window has the same rewind problem everywhere, it is only masked by a zero null block) and handles the prompt shapes that only Mamba used to reach (mixed token-id / embeddings prompts, a cut inside a multimodal item, push and Mooncake zero-token loads). DeepSeek-V4.1 is text-only and needs none of those.
Not a duplicate
#59142 (draft, opt-in, Mooncake only) moves replay to prefill and certifies checkpoints; this PR drops the replay of KV that P/D already transfers, for any connector that declares it, with no new config. #58504 keeps partial external hits exact by retaining the boundary block; loads carrying the window skip the rounding here.

With block size 64 and SWA window 128, we also tested exact token lengths around the suspected full-hit boundary:

At 1023/4095/8191 (prompt_tokens % block_size == block_size - 1), Prefill succeeded but Decode returned HTTP 400 because the logits contained NaN. After a full KV load, this PR skips replay but still rewinds one token for sampling; the resumed query then needs the token at N - 128, whose SWA block has already been retired.
The smallest safe fix appears to be retaining at least one additional historical token for replay-enabled SWA specs on both Prefill and Decode. Decode-only retention cannot recover a block already discarded by Prefill. This boundary issue does not directly explain the aligned 4096/8192 performance results.

vllm-project/vllm#59229 · ZJY0516 · MERGED · created 2026-09-29T14:03:53Z · merged 2026-10-02T12:58:36Z
Purpose
Kimi-K3 has no end-to-end prefix-cache coverage. FlashKDA exports Mamba prefill checkpoints, a path the Qwen3.5-based test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py never takes, so regressions such as the dropped prompt-end checkpoint fixed by #59146 / #59175 reach users unnoticed. KV offload, P/D and DCP are not tested with K3 at all.
This adds tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py. It serves riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy (the official Kimi-K3 config with 8 layers and no weights) with --load-format dummy, and runs 3 turns where each turn extends the previous prompt. Each turn must:

hit at least the previous prompt’s end checkpoint (cached_tokens), and
produce the same greedy tokens as a recompute of the same prompt under a fresh cache_salt (check_logprobs_close). This catches restored state that is wrong even though the hit count looks right.

With offloading, GPU prefix caches are reset before each turn, so the hit has to come back from CPU.
Every deployment runs in 4 modes:

block: Mamba-block granularity.
partial: --prefix-match-unit 128, i.e. partial hits.
block-dspark and partial-dspark: the same, plus DSpark speculative decoding as in the recipe. The draft is riverclouds/Kimi-K3-DSpark-for-8L-dummy, which is Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark with target_layer_ids remapped to the 8-layer target and no weights. With EAGLE-style block drop, the expected hit is one unit lower.

block: Mamba-block granularity.
partial: --prefix-match-unit 128, i.e. partial hits.
block-dspark and partial-dspark: the same, plus DSpark speculative decoding as in the recipe. The draft is riverclouds/Kimi-K3-DSpark-for-8L-dummy, which is Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark with target_layer_ids remapped to the 8-layer target and no weights. #59392 [Bugfix][Attention] Fix FlashInfer MLA DCP decode on ragged spec-decode batches
vllm-project/vllm#59392 · ZJY0516 · MERGED · created 2026-09-30T08:06:04Z · merged 2026-10-27T23:59:59Z
Purpose
Fix vllm-project/vllm#59065
With DCP > 1 and speculative decoding, FlashInfer MLA decode crashes when the decode batch is ragged, i.e. requests carry different numbers of query tokens. That happens whenever a request has fewer drafts than the others, and also during warmup. For example, Kimi-K3 with -tp 2 -dcp 2 and DSpark fails at engine startup:

ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)

Here a 1+7 request and a 1-token request make 9 decode tokens.
DCP cannot take the compact ragged path (cum_seq_lens_q), because it needs LSE. So ragged batches fall to the “uneven length” branch. That branch has two problems:

Shape mismatch. It splits q into one row per token, but it keeps block_table, seq_lens and causal_seqlens_kv_global per request. FlashInfer then rejects the call.
Silent wrong reshape. The branch is only taken when num_decode_tokens % num_decodes != 0. A ragged batch whose token count happens to divide evenly (e.g. 8 + 2 tokens) is instead viewed as a uniform 5 + 5 batch, and each request’s rows attend to the wrong KV.

Fix
A batch is now treated as ragged when num_decode_tokens != num_decodes * max_query_len. Ragged causal batches are split into single-token rows:

block_table and seq_lens are expanded per row with the existing _flattened_decode_metadata.
Each row’s DCP bound is T - (tokens of its request after it). FlashInfer defines causal_seqlens_kv_global as the global exclusive causal bound of each row’s newest query token, and dcp_tot_seq_lens (T) already includes all of the request’s query tokens.

The non-DCP causal path is unchanged; it already goes through cum_seq_lens_q.

vllm-project/vllm#59443 · mjkvaak-amd · MERGED · created 2026-09-30T14:13:00Z · merged 2026-10-05T10:40:03Z
Purpose

NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config QuarkConfig
Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config handles None, FP8 and the ModelOpt configs, and raises for everything else. It came in with #57497 (PLE n-gram table CPU offload). Before that, the Quark checkpoint served normally, for example on nightly-cd10ed6f9.

#59528 [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
vllm-project/vllm#59528 · ivanium · MERGED · created 2026-10-01T01:55:26Z · merged 2026-10-08T20:44:05Z
Purpose
Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not PAD_SLOT_ID: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as “no ring”, so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail: _kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel maps every token to block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool. Its torch fallback does the same.
Qwen4 QSA circular ring: circular_qsa_slot_mapping and _build_qsa_metadata_kernel map tokens to block_table[req, 0] and kept every block >= 0. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.
This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
Changes

vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block > 0.
Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes _make_block_table in the AMD pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. For the kpool tail, the existing CPU padding test now ends with a padding request on the null block, and the existing Triton-vs-CPU test adds a mixed batch and an all-null dummy batch. Both check that the null-block request maps to PAD.

Not a duplicate

#58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
#57158 zeroes block 0 after capture. That does not cover DP idle-rank dummy batches during serving.
#57169 and #59297 move the kpool tail onto CircularBufferSpec / the packed layout but keep its slot kernel unchanged.
#54296 masks out-of-range block indices in the generic slot mapping kernel, which neither ring uses.

#59532 [Perf][DSv4.1] Run decoder replay layers in CUDA graphs and trim in PIECEWISE graphs
vllm-project/vllm#59532 · Juntian777 · MERGED · created 2026-10-01T03:09:16Z · merged 2026-10-06T05:11:45Z
Purpose
Run the decoder-side SWA bounded replay layers (#58132) in CUDA graphs of their own, and trim them in PIECEWISE graph steps too. #58132 trims layers 21-39 to each prefill’s last 128 tokens only on eager steps (above the model graph’s capture range) and runs them eagerly there; those steps are often launch-bound (#58132 measured ~175 ms of kernel launches with the GPU waiting on a single 4K-8K prefill), and with a large max_cudagraph_capture_size nothing trims at all.

DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager (nvidia/decoder_replay_cudagraph.py), a CudaGraphManager owned by DeepseekV41ModelState, captures breakable PIECEWISE graphs of the replay layers, keyed by the replay batch’s padded token count and reading the layer inputs from static buffers. Attention runs in their eager breaks: the replay batch mixes prefill tails and decodes, and the SWA and sparse MLA builders support uniform batches only.
PIECEWISE model graphs of at least compilation_config.decoder_replay_trim_threshold padded tokens (768 by default) break out to the replay layers, which run on a replay batch (trimmed, or whole when nothing trims) and write their outputs to fixed buffers the graph’s next segment reads. FULL graphs and smaller PIECEWISE ones keep the layers on the whole batch, as before.
_prepare_replay_batch pads the replay batch to the smallest graph that fits the largest DP rank’s replay batch and sets it on DecoderReplayLayers as one ReplayBatch (rows, forward context, graph runner). A replay batch above max_cudagraph_capture_size, possible only in eager steps, stays eager.
Captures run the runtime path on a dummy batch, so the graphs read the buffers a real step’s replay batch fills; on MRV2 the SWA KV insert stays inside the graph and reads the slot mapping by address.
ModelState.capture_inner_cudagraphs is a new hook the runner calls after the model’s capture; it is a no-op by default.
On by default with breakable piecewise graphs (the default for DeepSeek-V4.1); compilation_config.cudagraph_decoder_replay=false turns it off. Also off under LoRA, prompt embeddings or on a non-first PP rank. Off keeps #58132’s behavior.

No open PR runs the replay layers in graphs. #56752 (closed) captured them nested inside the model graph’s capture; this captures them on their own and has the model graph break out to them.
Benchmark
Prefill-only TTFT of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 at f21ea3c947 (the last commit only adds the switch and renames), default CUDA graph settings, max_num_batched_tokens=16384, prefix caching off, max_tokens=1. With the default capture range every 1K-128K prefill step is eager, so this measures the eager path, not PIECEWISE trimming. Median of 3 runs in ms; c1 is one request at a time, c8 is 8 concurrent. Off is --no-swa-bounded-replay; parent is df8fd42 (main with #58132) with bounded replay on. Each topology ran all three on one node.

Why TP4 gains at long prompts and DEP2 does not
A profile of one 128K prefill shows the trimmed layers need only a few ms of GPU per chunk, but on TP4 their eager launches take several times longer and layers 0-20 do not hide them, so the GPU sits idle through most of layers 21-39; in graphs that idle time is gone. A DEP2 rank runs layers 0-20 on the whole chunk without TP splitting, so the CPU is far ahead of the GPU and the eager launches were already hidden; this PR only helps DEP2 where the step is short (1K-4K).

Overview
Projection fusion. Merge Qwen4Exp QSA’s QKVG and replicated indexer Q/K projections into one GEMM. LoRA keeps separate projections with standard linear dispatch.
GEMM dispatch. LL-GEMM for merged GEMM

SM103 (GB300): TP4 shape, done by me
SM100 (B200): TP4 contributed by @namgyu-youn
SM90 (H200): TP4 contributed tuning for M=1/2/4
SM121 (GB10): TP1 contributed by @stecasta
Also prune obsolete merged-HC and separate-QSA plans;

Prepare kernel. Support strided merged outputs and widen row-offset arithmetic to i64, with no noticeable performance difference in GB300 checks (≤1% in repeat measurements).

One GB300, BF16, TP=4: X=[M,2560], separate weights [3584,2560] + [640,2560], merged weight [4224,2560]. #59591 [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Store only the current rank’s shards in latent MoE up-proj
vllm-project/vllm#59591 · kliuae · MERGED · created 2026-10-01T10:51:08Z · merged 2026-10-08T14:55:21Z
Purpose
On the ROCm path, the routed up-projection in Kimi-K3’s latent MoE is built as a ReplicatedLinear where each rank holds the full weight. However, the fused tail’s ROCmLatentMoERunner doesn’t need the full weight. Instead, each rank consumes its own shard of up-projection weights, in a column parallel manner, and then a later all-reduce puts the slices back together.
At TP=8, this means that 7/8 of the weights, despite resident on the HBM, is never touched in the fused latent tail path. Across Kimi-K3’s 92 MoE layers, this constitute to ~3.9GB per rank of HBM consumed by unused weights, and takes spaces away from useful pools like KV cache.
This PR addresses this by storing only the shard that each rank needs for the latent MoE up-projection, using ColumnParallelLinear instead. The computation stays the same as the old fused latent path was already doing the same weight-shard extraction in the live path, and ColumnParallelLinear’s weight loader loads only the per-rank shard that it computes on.
In agentic workloads, the saved space from model weights increases the prefix cache pool and hit rate, and improves throughput by ~0.9-30% across concurrencies when KV cache constitutes a binding constraint.

[Bugfix][Spec Decode] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 NVFP4: keep ignored MTP/DSpark experts on MXFP4
Purpose
With nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4, DSpark speculative decoding accepts no draft tokens. Acceptance length is
1.00 (0 of 604,200 draft tokens on GSM8K), against 3.57 for the same speculative config on
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Speculation then only adds overhead. With this fix NVFP4 + DSpark is 2.3x faster at
concurrency 1 and 2.0x at concurrency 8 on MT-Bench, close to the native checkpoint.
No error is raised and accuracy is unaffected, since every draft token is rejected. The only hints are a warning right
after the draft loads (log from v0.30.0):

WARNING [modelopt.py] w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected.

and that the draft never logs Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
Root cause. ModelOpt NVFP4 exports of DeepSeek V4/V4.1 quantize the target’s routed experts and keep the modules in
quantization_config["ignore"] in their native format:

WARNING [modelopt.py] w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected.

and that the draft never logs Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
Root cause. ModelOpt NVFP4 exports of DeepSeek V4/V4.1 quantize the target’s routed experts and keep the modules in
quantization_config["ignore"] in their native format:

"moe_quant_algo": "NVFP4",
"ignore": ["*.attn.*", "*.ffn.shared_experts.*", "head", "mtp.*"]
So the bundled MTP/DSpark layers (mtp.*) of nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 stay MXFP4. Its
model.safetensors.index.json stores them as weight/scale, the same as the native checkpoint, not with NVFP4’s
weight_scale_2/input_scale.
DeepseekV4FP8Config.get_quant_method nevertheless returned ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE for every RoutedExperts layer
whenever moe_quant_algo == "NVFP4". That includes the draft layers, built as layers.{num_hidden_layers + k} in
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py. Loading then goes wrong without an error:

The packed 4-bit weights have the same shape as NVFP4’s, so they load.
NVFP4’s block-scale parameters are larger, and the MoE weight loader narrows them to the checkpoint shape, so half of
each is never written.
The NVFP4-only per-tensor scales (w13/w2_weight_scale_2, w13/w2_input_scale) have no counterpart in the MXFP4
checkpoint, so they keep their uninitialized torch.empty values. The warning comes from comparing the two halves of
the uninitialized w13_weight_scale_2.

matches it (fnmatch) keeps Mxfp4MoEMethod. Draft/MTP layers, built as layers.{num_hidden_layers + k}, are matched
under their checkpoint name mtp.{k}. Everything else keeps the previous behaviour: target experts, draft layers that are
not ignored, checkpoints without an ignore list, and non-NVFP4 checkpoints.
